summary: # Marvelous Designer Live Stream: Little Bee Military Uniform Production p06 ## Introduction In this live stream, we focus on the production of hat accessories for the Little Bee military uniform using Marvelous Designer software. We also address various technical aspects and answer viewer questions throughout the session. ## Hat Production Next, let's do the hat. Because the hat and the body are not intertwined, we can directly anti-activate the body board and then individually activate the hat board. In this way, the operation speed is faster. ### Hat Board Functionality Here, we have a small function. Sometimes, the hat board we made is not able to conform properly; it may be too close to the head, too round, or very flat. When we made the hat, did I make this hat very flat? The board is not intertwined. Why does the effect of my sewing seem closer to the head than this? ### Physical Properties Adjustment Do you know which physical properties I adjusted? Well, I guess you probably don't know, because only those who are serious about watching our physical properties teaching videos will understand. What kind of pressure? How come there is pressure? It’s funny; pressure is not a physical property. In fact, it is a deformation. I mean the position of the seam line. We are about to witness a miracle. When we reduce the deformation rate to 100, the wrinkles in the seam line position suddenly disappear. Isn't it amazing? ### Explanation of Deformation Rate When a fabric's deformation rate is adjusted to 100, the wrinkle effect of the seam line position will disappear. To explain it seriously, it’s not that the deformation rate is 100; it's that the properties of the wrinkle position differ from those of the flat fabric. The wrinkle position has various forces forming a wrinkle, like a small mountain, whereas the flat surface is, well, flat. How to control it? It's controlled by the deformation rate. When the deformation rate is 0, it forces all the small mountains and all flat surfaces to have the same properties. If your deformation rate is 100, it requires all those small mountains and flat surfaces to start deforming. ### Impact of Deformation Rate If the deformation rate is 0, the wrinkle intensity of the fabric will become very low. All the small mountains will be flat. You can understand it like this: 100% of the small mountains will be flat. If the deformation rate is 0, all the small mountains will not deform, making all the wrinkles more obvious. ### Visual Explanation Let’s visualize it. Assume we have a board that looks like this. Let’s freeze it. We have a small mountain, and we have a board sewn together with it, which has many wrinkles below. Is it possible to make clothes that are not easy to detach when making a natural look? If you transform it into a green state and set it to 100, when set to 0, all the wrinkles will be visible. The default mode is 80, where there is some shaking, but not much difference because it has not changed yet. ### Understanding Bending Intensity When the deformation intensity is set to 0, all bending intensity at the wrinkle position becomes zero. If it is all 0, it becomes very soft and has no bending intensity at all. When I set the deformation intensity to 100, the most obvious effect is that your sewing line position becomes very flat. However, the wrinkles in other positions also become very fine and soft, understand? ### Key Takeaways Everyone must pay attention to the deformation intensity, not just the deformation rate. Setting it to 100 can weaken the fabric significantly unless you need that special effect, like with our hat. ### Fabric and Edge Considerations For the edge, we also set the deformation rate to 100. When set to 100, it easily deforms, leading to curling at the edge. Therefore, we need to apply another fabric to it. We can’t let its deformation rate be 100; otherwise, it will encounter the same problem as before. ## Transition to Shoes Now, let’s shift our focus to the shoes. A long time ago, we shrank the foot into a narrow board to make it easier to wear boots. Before wearing boots, we need to add a fixing pin and then fix all the foot panels to the ankle of the simulation model. ### Fixing Pins When wearing boots, remember not to add boots first. Just place them on the ankle, then select the fixing pin and right-click to attach all the fixing pins to the simulation model. ### Compatibility with Downloaded Shoes In our software, the shoes you downloaded will adapt only to the simulation model. If you’re wearing shoes, you can use OBJ to simulate the model. The position of our boots inside includes the fixing pin, which holds all the material in place. ### Internal Material Considerations The internal net of the boots can turn into a hairline if you want to wear it. It can be troublesome, so we usually use the fixing pin to secure it to the simulation model. ## Gloves and Buckles Let’s discuss the gloves. The gloves are what we used in the motorcycle suit, and you can download the material directly. ### Buckle Attachment The buckle is straightforward. If we insert it into the virtual model or into the accessory, it’s all okay, as long as you don’t stick it onto the material. I use the water-water tool here for quick positioning. ### Coordinate Systems I switched the form of our positioning ball from world coordinates to regional coordinates. The screen coordinate is based on your current screen, while the regional coordinate is based on the model’s original coordinate system. ### Additional Adjustments In order to facilitate the rotation of this file, I switched to part coordinates, making it easier to work with. ## Wrapping Up This concludes the content of this episode about the soldiers. What problems do we have? Do you have any questions regarding our software? ### Viewer Engagement Thank you for your support! Our live broadcast covers a lot of topics, and I aim to prepare useful materials for everyone. After watching this tutorial, you can try making this set of clothes! ### Homework Assignment I want to see what software you usually use. Let me know what model the outer model will fall into, so we can arrange it accordingly. ## Conclusion Thank you for your support and for staying with us through the live broadcast. Remember to follow our channels for more tutorials and updates. If you have any questions, feel free to reach out through our QQ group or other platforms. ### Goodbye Thank you all for your support! I hope today’s content can help you. See you next time! Bye-bye!
